title: Antoni Augustyn Deboli → King Stanisław August, cipher despatches from St Petersburg, 1788 (older-code despatches)
correspondents: Antoni Augustyn Deboli (Polish envoy at St Petersburg) → Stanisław August
shelfmark: AGAD Warszawa, Zbiór Popielów (zesp. 12), sygn. 428

links.label: Letter list with scan links, ZbPop 428

status: AGAD inventory: "Korespondencja polityczna tajna (pismo cyfrowe) ... Listy zapisane szyfrem"; no decipherment noted. Keys in the same fonds: ZbPop 444 "Cyfra polska posłana do Petersburga Deboliemu" 8 III 1783; 451 "Chiffre François Nouveau envoyé a Monsieur Deboli" 1780; 453-454 the Cabinet's numbered keys 1772-1795 (not seen online). Not on DECODE (list dump searched); not in repo (known.py Deboli, Popiel: no hits). Scans online on AGAD's own image server. 27 Oct 2026 (targets/deboli1790/): attempted. The 1788 volume uses two codes. From the spring, despatches begin with 4000 and use the 1789-91 Polish code; their decipherments are the same-date Polish texts in ZbPop 417 (20 May pair aligned: 360 = o, 1657 = z). The earlier despatches are in an older code (groups to about 2450). ZbPop 417 has same-date copies for them too, but the 11 Jan pair did not align on its opening lines (homophones likely). Open: the older-code despatches, Jan to spring 1788 (and the older-code parts of later ones).
why: The Polish envoy's secret reports from Catherine II's court to the King during the Four-Year Sejm and the Russo-Turkish war; the ciphered parts carry what he would not put in the open despatch.
language: Polish/French (unknown which; the clear despatches of the same days are in Polish)

title: Bazaine and Castelnau → Napoleon III, Mexico, French cipher cable of 373 cable words intercepted by Sheridan's telegrapher Charles A. Keefer, never deciphered
correspondents: Marshal François-Achille Bazaine and General Castelnau → Napoleon III (copy sent by Charles A. Keefer → Gen. U. S. Grant)
date: 3 Dec 1866 (copied at New Orleans c. 9-17 Dec 1866)
shelfmark: Keefer to Grant, New Orleans, 17 Dec 1866, William H. Seward Papers (University of Rochester), Library of Congress microcopy roll 98 (Weber, Masked Dispatches ch. 17 nn. 46, 60)
folio_note: 373 cable words of a French numeric code (groups like 2209 613 562 273 15 2214, Weber n. 46) copied by Keefer from the line; plain text of the same message printed by Georges Girard, La vie et les souvenirs du général Castelnau (Paris 1930), pp. 117-118
status: Weber (Masked Dispatches, 3rd ed. 2013, pp. 114-116 and n. 63): Keefer 'could not decipher it' and hoped for the plain text from a French newspaper; 'There is no evidence Keefer ever solved the French cipher.' The plain text was published in 1930, so the content is known; the French cipher system itself was never reconstructed. Not in the repo (known.py: Keefer, Bazaine no hits).
why: A rare surviving ciphertext of the French numeric diplomatic/army code at the end of the Mexican intervention, with a published plaintext: a known-plaintext rebuild of part of the code that could then read Keefer's other French intercepts of Dec 1866.

title: US minister at Vienna → Secretary of State, cable in the 1867 State Department code with the code letters run together, 'never deciphered'
correspondents: US minister at Vienna (Henry M. Watts 1868-69 or John Jay II 1869-75; unknown) → Secretary of State (Seward or Fish)
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Telegrams received by the Department of State (1867 code period; Entry 209 'State Department Telegrams 1867-1869' cited by Weber) or Despatches from US Ministers to Austria (M46); exact item not identified
status: John Haswell to Hamilton Fish, 8 Jul 1873 (Fish Papers reel 95, LC), quoted by Weber, Masked Dispatches pp. 106, 131: cables from Turkey (decoded by J. C. B. Davis after long labour), Paris and Vienna arrived as strings of connected code letters; 'the latter one was never deciphered'. The 1867 code (letters and groups of unequal length, telegraphers merged them) is known (Weber 1979 prints it). 27 Oct 2026 (targets/vienna1873/): attempted; closed unread. Weber, Masked Dispatches pp. 106, 131 (Haswell to Fish, 8 Jul 1873) gives no date, sender or archive item for the telegram; the full 1867 codebook was not found online. Needs NARA RG 59 telegrams / M46 and the Fish Papers reel 95.
why: A State Department cable that was never read in its own time; with the 1867 code known it is a segmentation problem, and it would show what the Vienna legation reported in the late Seward/early Fish years.

status: Cryptoole XX1654-1 (open). Cryptiana unsolved.htm and louisxiv0.htm ('Prince of Condé (1654-1655)'): the 1654 letter f. 98 seems undeciphered and in a different cipher from the known 1655 Condé–Barrière cipher (f. 108); whether f. 101 reads with the 1655 key is untested. No validated diacritic-preserving reading established.

title: English royalist letter in numerical code, September 1645 (SP 106/10 f. 251)
correspondents: Unknown sender → unknown recipient
shelfmark: TNA, State Papers, inv.nr. 106 box 10, f. 251 · DECODE R931
status: Attempted, open (21 Sept 2026; own entry sp106r931 since 14 Oct 2026). Of the four DECODE records first grouped here, R722 is the 1625 Venetian letter of the SP 106/10 codebreaker's file (now sp106r722, catalogue 66) and R656 and R662 are that codebreaker's worksheet and memorandum on it. shelfmark: ASMo, Ambasciatori b. 4/23, 1, Envoy reports, Ferrara

title: Murberg, Johan, Görtz, Georg Heinrich von to unknown recipient
correspondents: Murberg, Johan, Görtz, Georg Heinrich von → unknown recipient
shelfmark: National Library of Sweden
status: DECODE R4350: Non-decrypted. Viewed 22 Sept 2026: the record is the whole Murberg volume (KB I.g.18, 114 images); the cipher is five passages (809 numeric groups 1-848, 175 distinct) inside a German peace memorandum of 1717 on Poland, the Czar and Norway (PDF pp. 34-41). No decipherment on the pages; the only Görtz key on DECODE (R7691, BL Add MS 32287 f.2, 1716) is a French 4-digit code, not this one. Ciphertext-only annealing (homophonic letter, alphabetical syllabary) failed, and failed its synthetic control. Needs Görtz's German chancery key (Riksarkivet Görtz papers). See targets/goertz1717/.
why: Ciphered letter of Murberg, Johan, Görtz, Georg Heinrich von to unknown recipient, 1717; what the cipher hides is not known.
